title: Fix once/off-during-emit semantics in the event emitter
prompt:
Our hand-rolled Emitter (src/emitter.mjs) misbehaves when listeners modify the listener list while an event is being dispatched. Required semantics (the same as Node's EventEmitter):

- emit(event, ...args) calls the listeners registered at the moment emit starts, in registration order; listeners added or removed during that dispatch only affect later emits. It returns true if there were listeners, false otherwise.
- once(event, fn) listeners run at most once, even if the listener itself (or an earlier listener) re-emits the same event synchronously.
- off(event, fn) accepts the original function for both on() and once() registrations; if the same fn is registered several times it removes only the most recently added registration.
- on() and once() return an unsubscribe function that removes exactly that registration (calling it twice is harmless).
- emitting 'error' with no 'error' listener throws: the argument itself if it is an Error, otherwise an Error whose message mentions it.
- listenerCount(event) reports the current number of registrations.

Run `node --test "test/*.test.mjs"`.
